title: Fix apply/rollback race condition causing mixed worker optimization states
author: Noah Patel
description:
Context: During the rollback gameday + a customer escalation (SUP-18503), we reproduced a race where an operator-triggered rollback could overlap with an in-flight apply stage. In certain interleavings, some workers would commit the new optimization config while others would revert to the previous version, leaving the fleet in a mixed state until the next periodic reconcile. This PR makes the runtime apply pipeline linearizable per (tenant, model, region) scope by introducing an apply-epoch token and CAS-style commit semantics at the worker checkpoint boundary.

What changes: (1) Control plane now includes a monotonic `apply_epoch` in the runtime apply intent payload; apply and rollback both bump epoch. (2) Workers persist the last committed (config_version, apply_epoch) and will only commit intents with epoch >= current; older intents are treated as no-ops and still ACKed for idempotent retries. (3) Apply pipeline checkpoint is updated so "download + validate" can run speculatively, but "commit" is gated on epoch comparison and a per-scope mutex to avoid mixed state inside a worker when concurrent reconciles fire. (4) Rollback now cancels any in-flight apply for the same scope by bumping epoch and emitting a `rollback_supersedes_apply` marker used by the rollout controller.

Why this fixes the bug: previously the pipeline compared only config_version and assumed apply/rollback were mutually exclusive at the orchestrator. Under retries, controller restarts, or delayed worker polls, a stale apply intent could arrive after rollback and overwrite the rollback state on a subset of workers. With epoch monotonicity + CAS commit, stale intents cannot regress the committed state.

Tests: adds deterministic concurrency tests that simulate (a) apply and rollback crossing in time with delayed worker polls, (b) controller retry storms, and (c) partial apply followed by rollback while some workers are mid-download. The new tests fail on main and pass with this patch.

Operational notes: This is a backwards-compatible change with a safe default epoch=0 for older orchestrator payloads. After rollout, we should see fewer "mixed_version" warnings in runtime logs. This is a hotfix candidate for the Limited GA safe-apply flag cohort.

Follow-ups: a separate PR will plumb epoch through Console rollouts UI and add a metric dimension on `optcfg_apply_epoch` for debugging (not required for correctness).
commits: runtime/optcfg: add apply_epoch to apply intent and worker checkpoint schema
runtime/optcfg: CAS commit semantics + per-scope mutex during commit
rollout: treat rollback as epoch bump; mark superseded applies
tests: deterministic race regression harness for apply/rollback interleavings
docs: update internal comments + troubleshooting log messages
conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify the commit boundary? If download happens speculatively, do we risk extra GPU memory churn when a stale intent is dropped at commit time?

Noah Patel (author): Yep. Download/parse can happen, but we don’t touch the live applier state until commit. For KV/cache-related toggles the commit path is the only one that triggers invalidation. Stale intent is dropped before invalidation, so churn is limited to a small CPU-side parse + any staged blob fetch. Added a note in `ConfigApplier::CommitIfNewerEpoch`.
Sofia Ivanova (review): The mutex is per-scope per-worker. Does it block batching scheduler updates too long under retry storms?

Noah Patel (author): Mutex is held only around the commit section (epoch check + swap + metric emit). Download/validate happens outside. Worst case we serialize commit bursts, but commit is <2ms in perf tests. Added a benchmark comment and a micro-timing metric `optcfg_commit_duration_ms`.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add an explicit log + metric when we reject a stale intent so on-call can see this quickly during incidents.
Noah Patel (author): Added `optcfg_intent_rejected_total{reason="stale_epoch"}` and a single-line warn with scope + epoch pair. Also threaded the request_id when available.
Benji Okafor (review): Control plane serializer sets epoch=0 for older configs; any chance we accidentally treat new intents as stale if worker already has epoch>0 and controller restarts?

Noah Patel (author): Controller persists epoch in the rollout state; restart will reload and continue incrementing. If it can’t load, we fail closed (rollout pauses) rather than emitting epoch=0. Added a unit test for restart path in `rollout_controller.test.ts`.
Omar El-Sayed (review): One nit: ACK semantics on stale intent should be explicit in the RPC comment. Otherwise someone might “fix” it later.
Noah Patel (author): Done. Updated proto comment and added a short design note in the applier header.
Sean Gallagher (approve): LGTM. This aligns with gameday findings. Please coordinate backport if we’re cutting a runtime patch release for the cohort.
Sofia Ivanova (approve): Looks good. Thanks for keeping commit critical section small.
Omar El-Sayed (approve): Approved after changes. The regression tests are solid.

release_notes: Runtime: Prevent mixed worker states when apply and rollback overlap by adding apply-epoch CAS semantics; adds regression tests for concurrent apply/rollback and retry storms.
